# The ring of integers of a cyclotomic field over the rationals is generated by a primitive root of unity

Let $n \ge 1$ be an integer and let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero that is an $n$-th cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$: $K$ contains a primitive $n$-th root of unity and is generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by the $n$-th roots of unity in $K$. Let $\zeta \in K$ be a primitive $n$-th root of unity. Then $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]$ is the integral closure of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $K$: an element of $K$ is integral over $\mathbb{Z}$ if and only if it lies in $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]$. Thus $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]$ is the ring of integers of $K$.

## Sources

- Daniel A. Marcus, Number Fields, 2nd ed., Universitext, Springer, 2018, Chapter 2, Corollary 2 following Theorem 12, p. 26.
